fullPassage:
People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.

In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.

In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.

Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.

Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."

The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.

Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

③ experience: 주어 the island(그 섬)는 3인칭 단수예요. 그래서 동사에 -s를 붙인 experiences가 맞아요. experience는 수일치가 틀림 ←정답

④ evolved: 'have evolved' 현재완료(have + 과거분사) — 적절
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(the island) → 동사에 -s (experiences)

questions.passage: Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering ①<u>to subtract</u> a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is ②<u>rotating</u> slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is ③<u>spinning</u> faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been ④<u>causing</u> an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① to subtract → subtracting: consider(고려하다)는 뒤에 동명사(-ing)를 목적어로 취하므로 subtracting
det.analysis:
① to subtract — 'scientists are considering ① to subtract a single second(1초를 빼는 것을 고려하고 있다)'에서 consider(고려하다)는 뒤에 to부정사가 아니라 동명사(-ing)를 써요. 그래서 to subtract가 아니라 subtracting이 맞아요 → 틀려요 ←정답

② rotating — 'Earth is ② rotating slightly faster(더 빠르게 자전하고 있다)'는 be동사+-ing의 현재진행형, 적절해요.

③ spinning — 'Earth is ③ spinning faster(더 빠르게 돌고 있다)'도 현재진행형, 적절해요.

④ causing — 'This behavior has been ④ causing an increase(증가를 일으켜 오고 있다)'는 현재완료진행형(has been + -ing), 적절해요.
det.tip: consider(고려하다) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing). to부정사는 안 돼요 → subtracting

questions.passage: The origins of flags probably began with warriors ①<u>decorating</u> their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was ②<u>adopted</u> by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: is → are (Most of + 복수명사(flags)는 복수 취급)
det.analysis:
① decorating: 'began with warriors decorating their spears'에서 'with + 명사 + 현재분사' 구조 — 적절
② adopted: 'This practice was adopted by ~' 수동태(be + 과거분사) — 적절
③ is: 'Most of these national flags __ ~'에서 'Most of + 복수명사'는 복수 취급이라 is가 아니라 are가 맞음 ←정답
④ feature: 'They commonly feature ~' 복수 주어 They + 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: Most of + 복수명사 → 복수동사 are

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms ①<u>known</u> as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which ②<u>evolving</u> approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to ③<u>assimilate</u> carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then ④<u>released</u> oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: evolving → evolved (관계대명사절의 동사는 시제를 갖춘 형태여야 함)
det.analysis:
① known: 'organisms known as cyanobacteria' ~로 알려진(과거분사가 명사 수식) — 적절
② evolving: 'Cyanobacteria, which ___ approximately 2.7 billion years ago'에서 which가 이끄는 관계대명사절에는 시제를 갖춘 동사가 필요해요. 과거의 사실이므로 과거형 evolved가 맞아요. 진행형 evolving은 틀려요 ←정답
③ assimilate: 'allowed them to assimilate' allow + 목적어 + to부정사 — 적절
④ released: 'They then released oxygen' 주어의 과거시제 동사 — 적절
det.tip: 관계대명사 which절의 동사 = 시제형. which evolved(진화했다)

questions.passage: Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert' → 수줍음 덕분에 전문가가 됨 → 불일치
det.analysis:
① 아이디어를 현실로 옮길 기회를 줌: 'gives them the opportunity to bring ideas ... into the real world'와 일치
② 창의성이 어린 시절 내성적 성격에서 비롯됨: 'his creativity came from being introverted as a child'와 일치
③ 필요할 때만 고독을 찾으라고 조언함: 'seek out solitude, but only when we need it'와 일치
④ 수줍음 때문에 전문가가 되지 못함? ←정답(불일치): 본문은 수줍음이 없었다면 전문가가 못 됐을 거라고 했어요. 즉 수줍음 '덕분에' 전문가가 된 것이라 '되지 못했다'는 반대예요.
det.tip: Had it not been for his shyness ~ = 수줍음 덕분에 전문가가 됨

ch: 혼자 있는 시간은 아이디어를 현실로 옮길 기회를 준다.
워즈니악의 창의성은 어린 시절의 내성적인 성격에서 비롯되었다.
필자는 필요할 때에 한해 고독을 찾으라고 조언한다.
워즈니악은 수줍음 때문에 컴퓨터 전문가가 되지 못했다.

questions.passage: People often ①<u>omit</u> the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we ②<u>perceive</u> periods. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① omit=생략하다 ② perceive=인식하다 ③ change=바꾸다 ④ casual=격식 없는 → formal(격식 있는) (부적절)

④ casual: 격식 없는 상황에 '격식 없는(casual)' 말을 쓰면 어색하지 않아요. 어색함을 주는 것은 '격식 있는(formal)' 말이므로 casual은 문맥과 반대 ←정답
det.tip: 어색함을 주는 것은 '격식 있는'(formal) 말. casual(격식 없는)은 정반대

questions.passage: In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their ①<u>basic</u> food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all ②<u>lacked</u> the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① basic=기본적인 ② lacked=없었다 ③ suffered→enjoyed (부적절) ④ risk=위험
det.analysis:
① basic: 감자를 기본 식량으로 삼았다 — 적절
② lacked: 병과 싸울 능력이 없었다 — 적절
③ enjoyed: 아일랜드가 기근을 '즐겼다'? 많은 사람이 죽은 재앙이므로 '겪었다(suffered)'가 원문 ←정답

questions.passage: In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.
questions.stem: 화자는 우물 옆에서 자라는 작은 나무를 보고, 그 나무가 살 수 있다면 다른 나무들도 살 수 있으리라 생각했다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
